`relieverChangepoint` separates fitting candidate changepoint paths from
selecting a model and K. The appropriate selector depends on how the loss was
constructed.

## Selection map

| Situation | Recommended workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary mean, covariance, regression, exponential-family, NMCD, or fixed KDE-L2 loss | `cv.reliever()` |
| Ordinary lasso path | `cv.reliever(cpd_family = "lasso")` |
| Interval-adaptive cross-fitted loss | `select_by_run(..., run_type = "recv", cpn_crit = "loss")` |
| One homogeneous setting from a cross-fitted hyperparameter grid | `select_across_runs(..., run_type = "crossfit_homo_hyper", cpn_crit = "loss")` |
| Deliberately chosen information criterion | `select_by_run()` |
| Independent evaluation data | `select_holdout()` |

## CPSS outer cross-validation

For its supported families, `cv.reliever()` constructs sample-efficient CPSS
outer folds, evaluates candidate segmentations on held-out observations, picks
the minimum held-out loss, and fits the selected path once on all data. The
returned `full_data_fit` is therefore ready for downstream use.

The fixed-kernel KDE-L2 interface treats `kernel` and `bandwidth` as fixed
inputs and selects K. NMCD constructs its reference distribution from each
outer training fold. The lasso interface can jointly select normalized lambda
and K.

## Cross-fitted ReCV

Cross-fitted families return the interval-adaptive `recv` loss by default. Fit
the path first, then select K:

```r
fit_cf <- reliever(
  X = x,
  y = y,
  cpd_family = "lasso_crossfit",
  cpn_max = 5,
  dm = 15,
  cov_rate = 0.7,
  method = "SN",
  nfolds = 2,
  nlambda = 25
)

selected <- select_by_run(
  result = fit_cf,
  run_type = "recv",
  cpn_crit = "loss"
)
```

To select one hyperparameter jointly with K, request the homogeneous outputs
when fitting. The order of `loss_output_types` does not matter, but `"recv"`
must be included.

```r
fit_cf <- reliever(
  X = x,
  y = y,
  cpd_family = "lasso_crossfit",
  cpn_max = 5,
  dm = 15,
  cov_rate = 0.7,
  method = "SN",
  nfolds = 2,
  nlambda = 25,
  loss_output_types = c("recv", "crossfit_homo_hyper")
)

selected <- select_across_runs(
  result = fit_cf,
  run_type = "crossfit_homo_hyper",
  cpn_crit = "loss"
)
```

If either unpenalized ReCV rule selects too many changepoints, changing
`cpn_crit = "loss"` to `cpn_crit = "sic"` adds a `log(n) * K` penalty.

## Information criteria and hold-out data

`select_by_run()` applies a criterion separately to each stored path. `"sic"`
uses the stored additive loss directly, whereas `"rss_sic"` first applies the
log-RSS transformation. The latter may be preferable for an RSS loss when its
residual variance is unknown or potentially heterogeneous.

`select_holdout()` evaluates candidates on independent data. For a custom loss,
confirm that its external scoring rule has the intended statistical meaning.
